title: Terms-Setting Standard for Hardship Assistance Programs Offers
content:
This standard governs how the terms of a plan under the Hardship Assistance Programs are set when a request is offered or a benefit is applied.

## 1. The loan figures

Plan terms are computed from the loan as it stands on the decision date, recorded on the plan as the pre-plan installment, pre-plan rate, unpaid principal and remaining months (the loan due dates left through maturity).

## 2. First affected due date

The first affected due date follows the program's first plan due date rule.

## 3. Deferral programs

Short-Term Payment Deferral and Disaster Relief Deferral defer the number of installments the borrower asks for, from 1 up to the program's per-plan maximum and the lifetime limit, with no plan installment.

## 4. Reduced Payment Plan — retired clause

The clause under which the Reduced Payment Plan set a plan installment of the program's reduced payment percent of the pre-plan installment, rounded to the cent and not below the program's minimum plan installment, for exactly the program's plan months, is **no longer in force**. The Reduced Payment Plan installment is set under the current Reduced Payment Plan rule.

## 5. Temporary Rate Reduction Plan — retired clause

The clause under which the Temporary Rate Reduction Plan set the plan rate for its plan months and a plan installment equal to the level payment amortizing the unpaid principal at the plan rate over the remaining months (not below the minimum plan installment) is **no longer in force**. The plan rate and installment of that plan are set under the current Temporary Rate Reduction Plan rule.

## 6. Term Extension Modification

Term Extension Modification sets a modified rate of the pre-plan rate less the program's rate reduction points (not below the program's modified rate floor) and an extension of the program's maximum term extension months, shortened so the total term does not exceed the program's maximum total term; the plan installment for each trial month is the level payment amortizing the unpaid principal at the modified rate over the remaining months plus the extension.

*Hypothetical figures, with 3.0 reduction points, a 5.99 floor, a 24-month extension and an 84-month total:*

| Pre-plan rate | Pre-plan rate less 3.0 | Modified rate |
|---|---|---|
| 18.00% | 15.00% | 15.00% |
| 8.00% | 5.00% | 5.99% (the floor) |

| Original term | Original term plus 24 | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| 60 months | 84 | 24 months |
| 72 months | 96, above 84 | 12 months |

## 7. Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit

Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit sets the plan rate to the lower of the pre-plan rate and the program's plan rate. This rate clause remains in force.

The clause under which the benefit's installment was the level payment at that rate over the remaining months, and the clause under which the benefit ran from the military service start date until the end of service is recorded, are **no longer in force**. The benefit's installment and its duration follow the current Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit rules.

*Hypothetical:* a pre-plan rate of 9.00 percent against a program plan rate of 7.00 percent gives a plan rate of 7.00 percent; a pre-plan rate of 5.00 percent stays at 5.00 percent.

## 8. Charged-Off Settlement Plan

The clause under which the Charged-Off Settlement Plan set the settlement amount at the program's lump-sum percent of the charged-off balance for one payment, or at its installment percent, and the clause allowing 2 up to the program's most settlement installments, are **no longer in force**; the settlement amount and the number of installments a borrower may choose follow the current Charged-Off Settlement Plan rules. Still in force: each settlement installment is the settlement amount divided by the number of installments, rounded to the cent, with the last absorbing the difference; the borrower chooses one.

## 9. Fees

No program charges an enrollment fee.
